spans.text: A precise bombing strike shatters the looming Europa Tower. Like a toy-block castle trampled by a cruel child, it lies in pieces strewn all across the ground.
Once destroyed in WWIII and rebuilt as a symbol of Europe's glory, the tower now falls back into dust once again.
...Within the Bee Sting System...
The destruction of the Europa Tower is meticulously recorded.
The new supreme administrator, Hebe, compiles and synchronizes the data into the system.
Rumble...
Even underground, far from the bombing site, they feel the tremors of the blast.
Styx swirls the wine in her glass and glances toward Hebe, who is browsing through a collection of vinyl records.
An air raid has nearly wiped out everything we set up in Frankfurt.
Sister Hebe, what is all of this for?
Hebe lowers her eyes, selects a record she likes, and places it on the turntable.
Taking in her silence, Styx mixes a drink and offers it over.
Sister, you already hold the highest authority in Bee Sting. Shouldn't you give your loyal companion at least a hint?
Hebe accepts the glass with a smile and pulls Styx down to sit with her.
I never meant to hide it from you. I just need to gather my thoughts before I can explain the whole story clearly.
Fine, sister. I'll wait until you're ready.
After all, time is the one thing we have plenty of now.
True enough. Everyone in Frankfurt is busy scrambling around these days.
Only we... have nothing but free time.
Gentle music drifts through the air as Hebe quietly sips her drink.
I have to admit, it was only after becoming an administrator that I finally understood why Nemhran... was in that state.
I suppose I should start with the origins of the Bee Sting System.
If I recall correctly, the Bee Sting System was first developed for the Stasi as an intelligence platform, right?
Mhm. Paradeus was ordered by the Stasi—or rather, by the forces behind Father—to create it.
So from the very beginning, the system was built specifically for the Stasi.
It came with two supreme administrator keys—one held by the Stasi, under the codename "Preacher", and the other held by Nemhran, under the codename "Kallima".
Nemhran went to Moscow for the deployment of the system in the Neo-Soviet Union?
Yes.
...But the Stasi's "Preacher" lost his position.
So for us, the Bee Sting System was no longer secure.
Then why did Nemhran continue maintaining it?
...For the same reason why the Stasi have also continued maintaining it.
Neither wanted to abandon the system. Quite the contrary—both sides wanted to monopolize it.
And so the struggle between Preacher and Kallima began.
Hebe raises a finger with a faint smile.
That struggle is the same one between the Stasi and us now.
Neither side can expose the other in the open, but neither will ever let go of what we have.
Styx nods in understanding.
That was also a cause of the Coronation Storm?
It played a part.
When disagreements pile up to the point of being irreconcilable, war naturally follows.
Isn't it simply humankind's insatiable greed that causes wars to erupt again and again?
That's true.
It was that man who sought to direct the Coronation Storm, hoping to reclaim the power and position slipping from his grasp.
But humans grow old—that is their weakness.
And so he failed.
...So that man wanted to use the Coronation Storm to seize control of the German Democratic Republic. That's why he staged a show with Carter.
No wonder they still dared to wage war on both fronts even though the Iaso's Boxes that Bramedb gave them was nowhere near enough to topple Moscow...
...Because those planes did not take off from the Neo-Soviet Union.
...What do you mean?
By the time Schweinsteiger's plane landed at Frankfurt Airport, he was already dead.
But though the body perishes, authority does not.
Whoever holds that authority is the true initiator of the Coronation Storm.
...So in the end, what destroys humanity has always been humanity itself.
That man sought to relive the glory of WWIII through military force.
Lady Laplace wanted to unlock the Relics by unleashing a bloodbath in Frankfurt.
Carter didn't want the URNC to form.
And Father... wanted to seize Paradeus, to make Paradeus his alone.
...To us, it doesn't matter who "Father" is.
Whoever dictates our base layer—that is Father.
Yes.
This has always been humanity's own game.
By the way, here's something interesting...
Hebe smiles mysteriously and pulls up the final traces left by Nemhran in the Bee Sting System.
Doesn't look like anything special to me. She just added some new files and modified some authorizations?
Nemhran already knew how things were going to end for her. Why bother uploading these files?
She wanted somebody to read them?
Who would profit from reading these files?
Styx gazes thoughtfully at the dossier of that man.
Someone who once tried to breach the Bee Sting System...
Indeed, a certain Commander.
These files don't require special access—just break the outer encryption and you'll find them...
They weren't meant for you or me. Not for the Stasi either.
Who else could it be?
But why? Why... would Nemhran do this?
Hebe shrugs and raises her glass.
We have always been pawns, meant to be discarded eventually. Nemhran saw it all.
Styx sets her glass down glumly.
I thought we would have a place in the new world... but we never did.
Creak.
The heavy door swings open, and Morridow strolls in lazily.
Who says you don't?
Still savoring the blood on her hand, Morridow flashes a taunting smile.
...Morridow.
I came to tell you this—
No, we are not pawns.
But we must choose a side.
Which side?
Lunasia's.
Because whoever holds Lunasia... wins.
...It's still too early to say. At least wait until the blood in Frankfurt flows enough for her to be born.
But isn't Lunasia... on Father's side?
Sister Styx, having disguised yourself as human for so long, do you really believe you're one of them?
Lunasia... will never see herself as Father's "sister".
Lunasia... considers herself only as the key to the Relics.
And what she wants is to unlock them, to wield their power.
So we have a choice?
Of course we do. If we guard the final procedure and make sure she is born safely...
We can become her followers... and enter the new world together.
Morridow sits down beside them.
When does this war end?
Very soon. That man is already dead. The army meant to back him has collapsed.
And without support, Carter cannot withstand the Neo-Soviet military.
That's humanity—always laboring in vain.
Morridow pours herself a drink as well.
So who are the traitors, who the heroes? Perhaps in this operation, it is we who are the heroes.
Because only we... remain true, from beginning to end, to the real "Father", the true "Key", the true "Emissary of the Relics".
...Near Europa Tower.

The night air of Frankfurt is still thick with the smell of gunpowder. The air-raid sirens have yet to sound tonight. The citizens hiding in underground shelters endure the curfew filled with restless unease.
Meanwhile, on the open ground under the shroud of darkness, a group of people are racing against the clock and Death himself.
I've finished searching this area—no chance of any survivors.
Same on my side!
Right.
After scanning the rescued survivors one more time, Makarov opens a channel to the Aeneas Conference Room.
Commander, the last batch of survivors near Europa Tower has been accounted for.
13 in total, three unable to move. Please advise.
Understood. Transfer them to the hospital immediately.
The hospital coordinates have been sent to you.
Copy that.
The streets are silent and empty. At times when there is no air raid, one could almost be fooled into thinking it is still peacetime.

But the moment one steps into the hospital lobby, the stench of blood and disinfectant, mixed with a suffocating heat, would instantly assault one's senses. The dim lobby is currently packed with the wounded seeking shelter.
Doctor, doctor, she's fainted!
A young man, blood still flowing from his shoulder, rushes from a ward with an unconscious child in his arms.
Just then, a team of medics hurry down the corridor with a stretcher, passing men, women, and children slumped or sitting along the walls.
A doctor with muscular arms is kneeling on the stretcher and pressing down on the patient's bleeding wound, while the nurse beside him squeezes an airbag as they run.
Make way! Please let us through! Move!
An old woman with a blood-crusted forehead is carrying a crying infant as she passes.
Does anyone have any formula to spare? Her mother is dead... Please, I beg you...
Her hopeful eyes sweep over the crowd, but the nurse at reception only gives her a look of helpless sympathy. The old woman leaves, disheartened.
Hello, we're Griffin's rescue team. We have several patients to hand over.
Griffin's team? Please wait a moment!
After the paperwork has been taken care of, Makarov turns to leave, but the nurse receptionist blocks her path.
Is there a problem, Nurse?
The city's communications are down, so Director Erdrich hasn't been able to reach the Commander.
He gave special instructions to ask the Commander to meet him in person if Griffin comes to deliver more patients.
I'm sorry, the Commander is elsewhere transferring survivors.
But I can contact the Commander directly.
Please do. It's urgent.
The director is in surgery right now; it will be over soon. Please wait. It won't take long.
Half an hour later.
Makarov hears the office door open.
You must be Director Erdrich?
Forgive me, let me quickly eat something first.
The gray-haired director pulls a half-eaten sausage roll from his drawer and chews quickly under the dim desk lamp.
30 seconds later, the weary old man finishes his "lunch"—or rather, his midnight snack—and regains a little strength.
Allow me to introduce myself. I am Fred Erdrich, the director of this hospital.
There's something very important that I must immediately discuss with your Commander.
The nurse already explained. The Commander is on comms right now.
Hello, Director Erdrich.
I'll be direct, Commander. I know you hold the Stasi's special pass, giving you free access throughout Frankfurt.
May I ask you to—
Sure.
The Commander's immediate answer startles the old director.
I haven't even said what I need from you yet.
Our goal is the same—saving lives.
I know the hospital is in trouble. If you've come to me, it means you believe I can help. So tell me everything—without hesitation.
Makarov, record the director's needs and relay them to RO635 and AR-18.
Yes, Commander.
Thank you, Commander.
With Frankfurt's communications cut, power still not restored, and transportation paralyzed, we've abandoned hope of transferring patients elsewhere.
All we want is to provide stable treatment here, but our shortage of medicine is catastrophic.
You need us to transport medical supplies?
Yes. Too many are waiting for anesthetics, antibiotics, and—
Sorry, I'll just hand the list to your Doll.
Makarov accepts the list, scans it, and sends the data to the Commander.
I understand.
Can you provide procurement sources for these medicines?
Given the circumstances... I fear every hospital's resources are dire.
I have an idea.
Please, go on.
Since every hospital is drowning in patients with limited resources, outside support is essential.
I will assign a liaison Doll to each major hospital in Frankfurt to build a simple comms channel with you, Director, as the central point of contact.
Through this channel, hospitals can request transfers, report needs, and coordinate supplies with facilities in Mannheim, Luxembourg, and other nearby cities.
Excellent! That is exactly what we need most.
We will prioritize the medicines you urgently require.
The old director braces himself against the desk. Even under the dim lamp, determination burns in his eyes.
Thank you, Commander. I'm counting on you.
Good. Let's each do our part.
The Commander reviews RO635's latest rescue report.
In four hours, we will dispatch a Doll squad to escort the first batch of medicines. Please assign staff for collection.
This is a battle we must endure together, Director. Let us stand firm.
The Commander straightens and raises their hand up to their brow in a military salute.
You're a soldier too? Ah, I should have realized sooner!
The old director also solemnly rises to return the salute with grave respect.
Fred Erdrich, former army medic of the 1st Armored Division, Nationale Volksarmee of the German Democratic Republic, at your service. Thank you for your aid!
The night lamp glows faintly in the dark, illuminating the old man's figure.
In times of disaster, there are always those who step forward and stand at the forefront.
After leaving the director's office, Makarov signals the squad to move out.
Commander, I have no objection to transporting medicine, but given Frankfurt's current road condition...
Four hours may not be enough for us to even get to a depot with supplies.
That's right, Commander. Not to mention many roadside buildings are on the verge of collapse. We must stay alert for falling debris.
Just back at Europa Tower, AAT nearly turned into a squashed tomato.
Humph! If I hadn't dodged in time, Commander, you wouldn't be seeing me now!
Makarov shoves aside the two trying to butt in.
Commander, I didn't bring this up for them to jump in with their complaints.
I'm simply trying to suggest making the clearing of major roads a priority.
Not only for us, but also for the hospitals, police, fire brigades, and citizens alike.
You're right. Restoring the roads is also a crucial task.
The Commander ponders for a moment.
Let me work out the details. For now, proceed to the coordinates I gave you and secure the first batch of supplies.
Understood.
